title: orders-db latency spike after a deploy — intervention runs, but the fix doesn't hold

ground_truth.summary: orders-db is genuinely degrading — a background compaction has been running for hours and buffer-pool hit rate has been sinking. The v4.2.0 deploy is coincidental. Passive checks can't tell (elevated latency looks compatible with either story). The traffic-shift intervention correctly rules out the deploy — cohorts_uniform proves both versions are equally slow — but rolling back the deploy would NOT fix the incident because the deploy is not the cause. The 5xx rate stays elevated after the canary shift. The safety-envelope's auto_revert fires and the verdict is honestly recorded as unresolved-by-intervention. Distinct from INC-4478 (deploy IS guilty) — this is the mirror case.

customer_impact._note_for_authors: P1 — the incident is real customer pain (SLA breach, revenue path), but a lower blast radius than INC-4479's P0. High CIS should still route it correctly for urgency; the auto-revert failure path is the demoable moment.

seed_hypotheses.claim: orders-db is degrading under sustained load — a long-running background compaction has been slowing reads for hours. The app-side deploy is coincidental. The fix is DB-side (throttle compaction, wait it out).

predicted_observations.note: if the DB is the cause, IOPS/buffer/connections all read elevated
if the DB is at fault, app errors are dominated by upstream-wait timeouts, not application exceptions
if the DB is the cause, BOTH version cohorts see the same slow p95 after a traffic shift

same upstream-wait signature as the DB story — ambiguous
if the deploy is guilty, the new-version cohort stays slow while the old-version cohort recovers after the shift

prior._note_for_authors: Small, harmless-looking change. The diff will bias the deploy story (H2) exactly like a red herring — the reasoner should NOT stop at the diff alone.

DB is showing elevated iops in prior — but this is ambiguous. Could be caused by the DB itself OR by the deploy driving more work. Passive checks can't discriminate — this is why the intervention is needed.

payload.signature: DB compaction backpressure elevated app latency; deploy was innocent
payload.resolution: Waited for compaction to complete; deploy rollback was NOT needed.

probeable._note_for_authors: Distractor: pressure is elevated but BOTH hypotheses predict shows_pressure, so this probe's info-gain is 0.
Distractor: mixed_upstream_wait matches BOTH hypotheses, info-gain 0.

intervention_results._note_for_authors: THE CAUSAL TEST. Route 5% of traffic back to v4.1.0 for 60 seconds, then compare cohort p95. Both cohorts return uniform (~1800ms) — the deploy is NOT the cause. H2 is eliminated, but rolling back would NOT fix the incident. The DB is genuinely at fault (H1).

verification_result._note_for_authors: The intervention correctly ruled out the deploy, but did NOT fix the incident because the deploy is not the cause. The 5xx rate stays elevated (54.2 > band max 5.0). Auto-revert fires. The audit chain records: intervention_executed → verification_result(recovered=False) → auto_revert_triggered. Verdict provenance falls back to observational.
